page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 62125.29 and a PassMark CPU score of 55792.37, both placing in the top 25% tier. The processor supports AVX-512 and cryptography extensions like AES and VAES, contributing to a strong PassMark CPU encryption score of 51982.03. Memory performance is also notable, with a PassMark memory score of 2805.13 in the top tier, though large-block uncached memory read bandwidth remains in the average range at 168.6 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient, registering at 294.35 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits a high compute-to-memory ratio, making it highly resource-dense for CPU-bound tasks but potentially constrained for memory-intensive applications that require more than 2 GB of RAM per core. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. Qualitatively, the dedicated core allocation offers consistent compute performance without virtualization steal, making it cost-efficient for parallel processing workloads. It is suited for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, web serving, and small-scale LLM inference.
